facts.fact: Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, enacted 24 March 2021, sets conditions in Part X (sections 70-71) for sending personal data outside the Republic: data subject consent plus Commissioner-approved standard contracts or intragroup schemes, or a Ministerial prescription of permissible transfers on an adequate-level-of-protection test, or Commissioner approval of a transfer in necessity; sensitive personal data must stay in the Republic; the Act itself says it commences on a date the Minister appoints by statutory instrument, and the document gives no commencement date.

note: No fact on the use aspect: the Act only provides for the Commissioner to approve standard contracts and for the Minister to prescribe criteria by statutory instrument; it states none published or applied.
